subject: Validation of cholesky_factor_corr fails because matrix isn't lower triangular

messages.author: e808374824de43c9
messages.subject: Validation of cholesky_factor_corr fails because matrix isn't lower triangular
parts:
Hey Everyone,
First off, I just wanted to give my sincere thanks to the Stan developers. After having worked with WinBUGS and R2WinBUGS for the last couple of years, I was borderline afraid of running my very first stan code because my model requires a fair bit of coding, and I was not looking forward to sleuthing through the entirety of the Stan users mailing list group to decode some esoteric error messages. I'm happy to say that despite the fact that there were at least 15 different bugs in my code, the error messages were incredibly helpful and after only about an hour I was able to get the code compiled.

So I have a question regarding an issue which I'm sure is due to numerical instability. For reference, I want to run a multivariate spatial model. If you let T be the correlation matrix between two outcomes at the same spatial location, and H_i be spatial decay matrix for outcome i, then when you properly permute all of the outcomes at all locations the covariance matrix can be written as Sigma = sum_p T_p \kronecker H_p, where T_p is the outer product of the p-th column of the cholesky decomposition of T (sorry for the mouthful). 

I wrote a function to calculate this kronecker product (which I've verified), and I've provided some sample code below. This part of a larger stan file, so if more information is needed, I'd be happy to provide that. I've highlighted what appears to be the problematic lines of code in red below.

functions{
  //Sum of Kronecker Products for multivariate spatial outcome
  matrix kron_sum(int n_factors, int n_space, matrix M_1, matrix M_2, matrix T_decomp){
    //Define function
  }
}

data{
  int<lower = 1> n_factors;
  int<lower = 1> n_space;

  matrix[n_space, n_space] D; // Distance matrix
  vector[n_space*n_factors] mu_vec; //Vector of zeroes for GP
}

parameters{
  vector[n_factors*n_space] W_factor_z; // z ~ N(0,1) for stochastic representation of multivariate normal, i.e. W_factor <- L_Sigma*W_factor_z
  real<lower = 0, upper = 1> rho1_factor;
  real<lower = 0, upper = 1> rho2_factor;
  cholesky_factor_corr[n_factors] T_factor_decomp;
}

transformed parameters{
  cholesky_factor_corr[n_space*n_factors] Sigma_factor_decomp;
  Sigma_factor_decomp <- cholesky_decompose(kron_sum(n_factors, n_space, exp(-rho1_factor*D), exp(-rho2_factor*D), T_factor_decomp));
}

model{
  vector[n_factors*n_space] W_factor;
  vector[n_space] Wnew_factor[n_factors];

  rho1_factor ~ uniform(0,1);
  rho2_factor ~ uniform(0,1);

  T_factor_decomp ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(1);

  W_factor_z ~ normal(0,1);
  W_factor <- Sigma_factor_decomp*W_factor_z; // Stochastic representation of the spatial random effects vector
}

The error message I get (a bunch of times) is 

"Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:"        
"validate transformed params: Sigma_factor_decomp is not lower triangular; Sigma_factor_decomp[1,2]=2.122e-314"

If I manually recode Sigma_factor_decomp[1,2] to zero, then the above error message still happens, but with Sigma_factor_decomp[1,3] instead.

It seems pretty clear that the issue is that objects of type cholesky_factor_corr are supposed to be lower triangular matrices, but for some reason Sigma_factor_decomp's upper triangular elements are returning small, but non-zero values. 

First off, I find it a bit odd that this is happening since I'm explicitly defining Sigma_factor_decomp as a cholesky decomposition of some other matrix (I have already verified that my Kronecker product function is working as it should be), and I'm not sure what would cause any of the upper triangular elements to be small non-zero numbers. Assuming this is just some sort of numerical stability issue, should I just loop through all the upper triangular elements and manually set them to zero?

Thanks so much for any insights!

Quick Edit: I recall seeing something like this pop up on the forum a long time ago, but I can't remember where I saw it, so sorry if I am asking a question that has already been answered elsewhere.

Martin Flores

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Validation of cholesky_factor_corr fails because matrix isn't lower triangular
parts:
On Thursday, June 2, 2016 at 1:12:43 PM UTC-4, mjfl...@g.ucla.edu wrote:
First off, I find it a bit odd that this is happening since I'm explicitly defining Sigma_factor_decomp as a cholesky decomposition of some other matrix (I have already verified that my Kronecker product function is working as it should be), and I'm not sure what would cause any of the upper triangular elements to be small non-zero numbers. Assuming this is just some sort of numerical stability issue, should I just loop through all the upper triangular elements and manually set them to zero?

It is odd but the oddness can be overcome by recognizing that, when you declare in the transformed parameters (or transformed data) block

cholesky_factor_co{v,rr}[K] foo;

that does not *make* foo be a Cholesky factor but rather tells Stan to *verify* that it is a Cholesky factor. If you are sure that the definition of foo is theoretically a Cholesky factor (which is the case if it is just the output of cholesky_decompose), the solution is to tell Stan to not verify that by declaring

matrix[K, K] foo;
foo <- cholesky_decompose(...);

Ben
